video_title: Dwight Howard & Roscoe Dash On ATL Rap Scene & Lebron Going To Knicks If They Win The NBA FInals

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on the success of his song 'All The Way Turnt Up'
quotes.excerpt: I had every remix to every one, Soulja Boy, the remix with Trey Songs and Fabolous.
quotes.quote: I had every remix to every one, Soulja Boy, the remix with Trey Songs and Fabolous. I would play the 20-minute version. It got me so hyped before every game. It is a viral video of me doing that in 2009 before the finals of me turning up and dancing to that shit.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on his creative process and the 'See No Evil' mantra
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to be able to respond. I am a fire sign, I am an Aries.
quotes.quote: It was a lot of stuff going on. It kind of goes back to the motto of this show, too. Just seeing no evil, hearing no evil, and speaking no evil. For me, I wanted to be able to respond. I am a fire sign, I am an Aries, so naturally, the fire in me wants to respond to whatever is going on. But I thought it was a very interesting way to just let things speak for themselves and kind of just remain quiet.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on his selective approach to listening to new music
quotes.excerpt: I am already overly opinionated and I am a visionary for other people too.
quotes.quote: I am already overly opinionated and I am a visionary for other people too. So with that comes the discernment of being able to see what is actually going on. For me, I try to hear what the world thinks. It is good for me too as an artist for marketing ideas and things of that nature too. So I dissect it from multiple angles before I actually listen to it.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on the tactical nature of music industry contracts
quotes.excerpt: It is a tactic. And you know it is 2026, we are kind of making our own shit up.
quotes.quote: I have had my share of messed up contracts too. So, it is a tactic. And you know it is 2026, we are kind of making our own shit up as we go. Where as when me and you were coming up, it was a little bit more structured. We went through a whole bunch of different eras, so our etiquette is a little different.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on his early rap aliases and getting kicked out of school
quotes.excerpt: My name in there was PC Problem Child at the time. I was just getting kicked out.
quotes.quote: I went through a few names actually. My name in there was PC Problem Child at the time. I was just getting kicked out of school so it made sense. I got kicked out of eight schools. My mom will tell you this, I had a lot of time to sit and find something else to do that would keep me out of trouble.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on being misunderstood as a child and his creative outlet
quotes.excerpt: These kids are like gifted and they are different, and hypersensitive, which we all at some point.
quotes.quote: Now they call kids, they are giving kids like the autistic thing. But I think these kids are like gifted and they are different, and hypersensitive, which we all at some point were before we became dumbed down in certain aspects by whatever you consume. I was one of those kids. They tried to put me on the red lane when I was younger. Imagine what that would have done to my creativity.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on how he realized music could change his life
quotes.excerpt: I started like, we had a Dell desktop computer at home. I never forget this.
quotes.quote: I started like, we had a Dell desktop computer at home. I never forget this. I had a Dell desktop and I used to go get like the big 300 spool of CDs and like burn my music onto the CD. This is like Limewire age. I would take them to school, I was making my own stuff on Photoshop, my own like cover art or whatever. This is Blackout Boys time and I would sell my CDs for $5 at school. So once people started giving me $20 to hold the CD until Friday or something like that, that is when I knew like, oh hold on, I got something going on.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on the influential rap groups of his youth in Atlanta
quotes.excerpt: We had like Chito Gambine, we had hard hitters who ultimately ended up being Travis Porter.
quotes.quote: We had like Chito Gambine, we had hard hitters who ultimately ended up being Travis Porter. We had Black Mob and the Fam. These was all like the groups that I was listening to on MySpace when I was like, damn I need to make music. This is when I am competing with it. It is like this type of shit. So the YC stuff or the T-Bag that hole, all that shit, yeah that is that. That is that.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on his collaborative work with Kanye West
quotes.excerpt: My mom was like the other stuff that I got the ultimately became like the Marvin Gaye.
quotes.quote: My mom was like the other stuff that I got the ultimately became like the Marvin Gaye and Shardoneys and stuff like that. Like she taught me the Gerald Leverts and Luther Vandrosses, the Dion Warwicks, Brian McKnights, Barry Whites, all that stuff. But my brother, my brother was like Little John and the East Side Boyz, Pastor Troy, JT Money, Trick Daddy, Three 6 Mafia. We had all the we had all the VHSs. We had Reasonable Doubt on cassette too and Streets is Watching. We had the little cassette tapes for that too. So I am really embedded in the culture.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on the creative process behind his hit song 'All The Way Turnt Up'
quotes.excerpt: I was thinking I was playing with the knob at the time and I was like, oh.
quotes.quote: I was thinking I was playing with the knob at the time and I was like, oh, all the way turnt up. I started doing my hand like this. I was like, what if I just sang that? I think T-Pain had just dropped the autotune at the time. I was like playing with that and I just came up with it.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on the importance of independence in the music industry
quotes.excerpt: To me, man, honestly, it is about the years that it is that it is existed.
quotes.quote: To me, man, honestly, it is about the years that it is that it is existed in this capacity. You know what I am saying? Like this shit came out in like 2010, 2011. You know what I am saying? So it is reinvented itself multiple times. And when it came out, we didn't have TikTok and social media and shit like that. All we had was Twitter. You know what I am saying? So for it to like keep doing its thing and people making dances to it and literally on the RIAA certification thing, it is going to tell you the amount of years that it took to do it.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on his first meeting with Kanye West
quotes.excerpt: I think I did 'Rip the Runway' was my first B.E.T. thing.
quotes.quote: I think I did 'Rip the Runway' was my first B.E.T. thing. And that is when like all the kids from my school was like, hold on, that is Jeff on T.V. Like they was like, I know him. Like, they was like, that was my moment. My mom used to tell me all the time, like, turn that shit down. She was asking why I was taking her car every weekend and try to go to the club on the other side of town and bring it back with like all it was about miles then at that point. My mom like, you put 3,000 miles on my car, I ain't giving you my car no more. I am like, Mom, I really got to go get this song played this weekend. Like, you know what I am saying? So that was my moment whenever they were able to see it.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash and Waka Flocka Flame recording at Patchwork Studios
quotes.excerpt: I am telling Waka, I am like, bro you need a song that is like for the women.
quotes.quote: Me and Waka had been moving around a lot, but we never did no music together. I went up to Patchwork, this is around the time when Gucci had got out, and that shit looked like the club. I didn't know Drumma Boy was in there. Drumma was in there cooking up. Me and Waka was talking about some whole other shit, but whole time I am listening to Drumma at the same time. And I am telling Waka, I am like, bro you need a song that is like for the women. They love you, bro. So if you get a song for them, that is going to be like next level for you. So I was like just write the verse. And so, then I went in, he put them horns on. When them came in, I said, all right, I am ready to go. Waka just happened to be in the process of us talking. He is sitting over there on the Blackberry. I said, man tell the nigga to go in the booth, bro. We know who he is, put him in there. So he was on the phone cooking the whole time, bro. Quiet. He probably said like five words to us before he recorded that verse.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash recalls meeting Kanye West and recording for Cruel Summer
quotes.excerpt: I am like a 21, 22-year-old kid, meeting Kanye West in the room
quotes.quote: The Marvin Gaye and Shardoney story was crazy just because he was playing me shit like No Church in the Wild before he asked me to play some shit for the first time. And this is my first time meeting him. So like, I am like a 21, 22-year-old kid, meeting Kanye West in the room when Bentley Fonzworth and all these other people and a motherfucker is playing shit like that, 'Otis', motion picture, 'No Church in the Wild', and he is like, alright, unplug the shit, you play something. I am like, what the fuck you want me to play after that? But he ended up taking that is probably like the third song I played, and I went home and like two weeks later, it was a big Sean song.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on the collaborative process for creating timeless music
quotes.excerpt: if we all sit here and share stories, that is how we make timeless music
quotes.quote: That's probably my favorite collab moment because I learned so much from just like different ways to be able to create than what I was used to. Like round table settings, or being able to take a conversation that we are all having and be able to turn that into some music. And that's when I learned like, okay, no one person can tell an experience that everybody is going to be able to resonate with. But if we all sit here and share stories and put it in a space where it is more digestible for people, that is how we make timeless music. Perspective is everything. That is a science too.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on his songwriting process and hook writing
quotes.excerpt: I got 'Home' with Travis Scott, 'Feels Like Vegas' with Tinashe, uh, 'Fly Away' with LeCrae.
quotes.quote: I got 'Home' with Travis Scott, 'Feels Like Vegas' with Tinashe, uh, 'Fly Away' with LeCrae. Um, we have a slew of Metro stuff that just came out on the futuristic summer thing, uh, 'You Deserve', 'Butterflies', 'Slide', uh, 'Where You From', I like that. Um, all those were on the same project. I also did 'Pride and Joy' for Fat Joe and Kanye. That's the other record that came out that I forgot about. 'Mano', 'Let It Fly', um, damn, it is the list is so crazy, bro. I can't even remember all this shit. 'Oh My', 'So Many Girls'.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on his perspective on being a songwriter
quotes.excerpt: Mine can look a lot of different ways, honestly. I try to create all my music from that same space.
quotes.quote: Mine can look a lot of different ways, honestly. I try to create all my music from that same space. If I am being honest, I try to envision myself performing it, like I am at Made in America Music Festival or something. Like, what are people going to respond to? Then I think about if I am in the club, what are the girls going to get on top of the couches for? You know what I mean? Like I am thinking like that. So most of the time I am not even embodying the artist per se, unless it is something that is like particularly for them. But most artists don't even want to sound like themselves. They want to put themselves on a song that doesn't sound like them. That is the difference.

quotes.speaker: Roscoe Dash
quotes.summary_phrase: Roscoe Dash on the importance of authenticity and independence
quotes.excerpt: That's the sauce to Jazmine Sullivan or somebody is because they are inverting things.
quotes.quote: That's the sauce to Jazmine Sullivan or somebody is because they are inverting things that were existing in one other way and they are like, you know you could do it like this too, right? And the world don't always be ready for that.
